SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Ice melting to water

2. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.

4. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Only water vapour

5. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. newton (N)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. joule (J)

6. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Water always increases oxygen

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.

8. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Removing all vegetation

9. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A mixture of two liquids

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

13. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

15. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Primary consumers only

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
